terms.comment: The act of selling; in Cicero the sale of a man’s goods (bonōrum vēnditiō, Rosc. Am. 110). For sale is vēnālis (see for sale).

evidence: Cic. Att. 12.3; Plaut. Men. 5.9.91–94 (Lewis & Short: auctiōnem facere)
terms.comment: A public sale to the highest bidder, a crier (praecō) calling the bids (Lewis & Short).

venditio.html: From vēndō, contracted from vēnum dō (de Vaan 663, s.v. vēnum), as this lexicon writes it (see sell). Spanish keeps a close vowel: vendo, beside tiendo from tendō. Traupman prints vēnditiō (pp. 131, 373).

sources: Lewis & Short: venditio · Lewis & Short: auctio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 131, 373.
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), p. 663.
